claim: Official Receiver seeks to stay Mr Yuen's action pending investigation of the Agreement as to whether it was a sham, impeachable by the Official Receiver
requested_remedy: Official Receiver seeks to stay Mr Yuen's action pending investigation of the Agreement as to whether it was a sham, impeachable by the Official Receiver

facts.F1: Mrs Har Sio Ying (the Deceased) died intestate on 21st April 1989 leaving a flat (the flat) as part of her residuary estate.
facts.F2: The Bankrupt (Mr Law), son of the Deceased, was one of the next-of-kin.
facts.F3: Letters of administration have not been granted in respect of the Deceased's estate.
facts.F4: The Bank filed a petition for the repayment of a mortgage loan on the Deceased's two flats, which Mr Law was subsequently appointed as the personal representative to represent the estate.
facts.F5: Mr Yuen claimed to have bought the flat from the Deceased in 1983 and lodged an entry in the Land Register against the title in 1992.
facts.F6: The Agreement for the sale of the flat was not registered until 1992 and Mr Yuen commenced an action against Mr Law for specific performance of the Agreement.
facts.F7: An order was made for specific performance of the Agreement on 19th January 1993, but the Official Receiver seeks a stay of proceedings due to concerns about the validity of the Agreement.
facts.F8: The Official Receiver will further explore the bona fides of the Agreement and gather funds from the Bankrupt's creditors for the investigation.
facts.F9: The court allows Mr Yuen to apply to lift the stay of action on two days' notice.

lawsuit_type: Application under s.14 of the Bankruptcy Ordinance to stay proceedings
reference_issues: Whether the Bankrupt's entitlement to a share in the unadministered assets of the residuary estate as next-of-kin amounts to 'property' under the Bankruptcy Ordinance.
Whether the Official Receiver has jurisdiction to seek a stay of Mr Yuen's action under s.14 of the Bankruptcy Ordinance.
Whether the Official Receiver can impeach the Agreement as a sham or fraudulent transaction.
authorities:
Bankruptcy Ordinance, Cap.6, s.2, 14, 43, 53(4), 97
Re S.C.O.15 r.6A

claim: Recovery of a loan and vacant possession of the secured property
requested_remedy: Recovery of a loan and vacant possession of the secured property
parties: Defendant: The debtor's estate (D1) and the debtor's wife (D2)

facts.F1: The plaintiff entered into a loan agreement with Mr Leung, the debtor, on 24 December 2014 for a principal sum of HKD 6,600,000.
facts.F2: The loan was secured by a second legal charge against a property on MacDonnell Road, Hong Kong, registered in Mr Leung's name.
facts.F3: Mr Leung's wife, D2, executed a personal guarantee in favour of the plaintiff.
facts.F4: Mr Leung failed to repay the loan in full or any monthly instalments since the 16th instalment due on 24 April 2016.
facts.F5: The writ was issued on 21 August 2017 against Mr Leung and D2 to claim repayment of the loan plus interest, and vacant possession of the property.
facts.F6: Mr Leung was declared a mentally incapacitated person under the Mental Health Ordinance on 17 November 2016, and the Official Solicitor was appointed as the committee for Mr Leung's estate.
facts.F7: Mr Leung passed away on 20 May 2021, and the discharge of his legal aid certificate was filed on 31 May 2021.
facts.F8: The court ordered that the proceedings be continued as between the plaintiff and the estate of Mr Leung Pak Wai as D1, and granted leave to carry on the proceedings in the absence of a person representing D1.
facts.F9: No one appeared on behalf of D1 at the trial, and D2 was absent.
facts.F10: At the material time, Mr Leung was suffering from a mental disorder.

reference_issues: Whether Mr Leung had the requisite mental capacity at the time when he signed the Loan Documents on 24 December 2014
Whether the plaintiff had actual or constructive notice of Mr Leung's mental incapacity
Whether Mr Leung could rely on the doctrine of non est factum
Whether the execution of the Loan Documents was procured by D2's undue influence over Mr Leung, and if so, whether the plaintiff ought to have known of the same
authorities:
Mental Health Ordinance, Cap 136
Order 80 of RHC
Mental Capacity Act 2005 (UK)
Money Lenders Ordinance, Cap 163

claim: The plaintiff claimed that the mother (defendant) was breaching the court order and drinking alcohol when she had access to the child, not producing the breathalyser tests as ordered, and producing fake reports.
requested_remedy: The plaintiff claimed that the mother (defendant) was breaching the court order and drinking alcohol when she had access to the child, not producing the breathalyser tests as ordered, and producing fake reports.

facts.F1: The court had previously granted the father (respondent) leave to relocate to Japan with the minor child, A, who is now 8 years old.
facts.F2: The mother (applicant) had previously been resistant to all forms of supervision of her access to the child due to concerns about her alleged alcoholism.
facts.F3: The mother had undertaken not to drink alcohol when the child was in her care.
facts.F4: The father alleged that the mother had breached this undertaking and had drunk alcohol in front of the child.
facts.F5: The mother admitted to only partially complying with the court order regarding breathalyser tests and gave various reasons for this.
facts.F6: The father proposed changes to the breathalyser test arrangements, including having a monthly contract with the supplier, regular recalibration of the device, and more frequent testing.
facts.F7: The mother responded to these proposals, accepting some but rejecting others.
facts.F8: The father will relocate to Japan with the child at the end of the summer school term, and the child's habitual residence will become Japan.
facts.F9: The court considered the mother's previous breaches of the court order and her alleged alcoholism when making its decision.
facts.F10: The court considered the best interests of the minor as the first and paramount consideration, in accordance with Section 3 of the Guardianship of Minors Ordinance, Cap. 13.

lawsuit_type: Family law, specifically a miscellaneous proceeding under Section 10(1), 10(2), and 23 of the Guardianship of Minors Ordinance, Cap. 13
reference_issues: Whether the mother had complied with the court order regarding breathalyser tests
Whether the mother had breached her undertaking not to drink alcohol when the child was in her care
How to vary the access arrangements post-relocation to Japan
authorities: Section 3 of the Guardianship of Minors Ordinance, Cap. 13
